From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Sat, 16 Mar 2029 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Crestwell RFP - DPF questionnaire (initial)

Soojin / Laura — initial draft of technical answers below; I attached the controls extracts and a short runbook summary for key points. I focused on cross-border processing, KMS, and logging schema.

Highlights / proposed answers (short):
- Data flows: request routing defaults to region of request; for hosted customers we operate regional serving pools (us, eu). We can pin customer workloads to EU-only pools under a Private deployment or Dedicated with residency commitments; hosted API customers can request EU-only routing via a tenant flag (subject to contractual SLA).
- Cross-border transfers: we use standard contractual safeguards and technical controls (TLS in transit, at-rest encryption, per-tenant key separation). For processor-to-processor transfers (e.g., cache replication for HA) we restrict egress to approved regions and log all events to immutable audit logs.
- KMS: customer-specific KMS integration available (bring-your-own-key via KMS/HSM) for Dedicated and Private; hosted can use customer-managed keys on request for enterprise tier.
- Logs & evidence: we can provide anonymized token-level latency logs, audit trails for export events, and a CSV export of subprocessor list with regions.

Attachments: DPF_evidence_v1.pdf (controls extracts), runbook_kms_summary.pdf

Open items for Laura: exact DPA wording around transfer mechanisms (SCCs vs DPF + supplemental controls) and whether we commit to EU-only processing for the entire pipeline (model weights, training telemetry).

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference


From: Nina Kapoor <nina.kapoor@crestwell.com>
To: Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@crestwell.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Julian White <julian.white@counselfirm.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Mar 2029 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crestwell RFP - DPF questionnaire (follow-up)

Thanks Miguel — and thanks Ben for the quick draft. A few follow-ups from legal/tech:

1) We need explicit confirmation whether Redwood uses any external model providers or model hubs that would result in training or telemetry leaving EU boundaries for a EU-only tenant. Example: if we enable long-term conversation logging for model tuning, does Redwood store that data outside EU?

2) Please confirm the subprocessor list includes any third-party observability/metrics providers and their hosting regions.

3) For DPA annex wording: our legal team prefers to see a clause that guarantees EU-only processing by default for our account unless we explicitly request otherwise, and an incident escalation SLA for cross-border transfers. Can Redwood commit to that in Dedicated or Private?

We appreciate a consolidated response with the three items above by 20 Mar.

Regards,
Nina Kapoor
Head of Vendor Risk
Crestwell Therapeutics


From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Miguel Alvarez <miguel.alvarez@crestwell.com>, Nina Kapoor <nina.kapoor@crestwell.com>, Julian White <julian.white@counselfirm.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Mar 2029 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Crestwell RFP - DPF questionnaire (compiled response)

Hi Miguel / Nina / Julian — thanks for the questions; please find our consolidated response and attachments. We've tried to be explicit on the three points Nina raised. Summary:

- EU-only processing: For Dedicated and Private deployments we can contractually guarantee EU-only processing (covering inference, KV cache, and operational logs). For hosted tenants we offer EU routing flags and a model residency commitment for enterprise customers as a contractual option; we cannot guarantee EU-only processing for hosted free-tier tenants.

- External model providers / telemetry: Redwood does not send customer conversation logs to third-party model hubs for training without explicit customer consent. We offer opt-in telemetry for model improvement; telemetry ingestion is scoped per-account and can be disabled. Any telemetry or training telemetry for an opt-in tenant will be processed in the tenant's pinned region.

- Subprocessors and observability providers: full subprocessor list attached. Third-party metrics providers are used for aggregated service health telemetry; we can provide region-limited integrations and a contractual commitment to only use EU-hosted instances for an EU-residency Dedicated/Private deployment.

- Incident & escalation SLA for cross-border transfers: proposed DPA annex includes an escalation clause and 48-hour notification for any unplanned cross-border export events; for Dedicated/Private, we propose a contractual obligation to implement technical mitigations within 7 calendar days of identification.

Attached: DPF_evidence_v1.pdf, DPA_annex_draft.docx, runbook_kms_summary.pdf

Next steps
- Laura will follow up with the DPA annex marked for legal redline (cc'd).
- Ben will provide the CSV export of subprocessor regions and a short manifest of any planned cross-border replication events by EOD 21 Mar.

If this looks good, I can package everything into a single secure Drive link and send to your legal team (Julian) for review.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Account Exec
Redwood Inference
